title: introduce-stream-fragment-coordinator-and-deferred-toolcall-handshake
author: Marcus Valdez
body:
Summary:
Introduce a lightweight stream fragment coordinator in the streaming runtime to make SSE/EventStream chunking resilient to partial JSON emissions, out-of-order delimiter painting, and race conditions around function/tool-call handoffs. This PR adds a coordinator that: (1) tags fragment boundaries with stable sequence anchors, (2) defers toolcall handshake until fragment completion when boundaries are ambiguous, and (3) emits compact checkpoint markers that help clients resync without re-requesting tokens.

Motivation:
We continue to see intermittent customer reports of partial JSON objects in streaming responses when backpressure, connection truncation, or multi-threaded flushes occur. Current heuristics occasionally paint delimiters in a different order than tokens arrive, leading to malformed JSON at the client or duplicated tool calls. A robust server-side coordinator reduces client-side heuristics and eliminates several edge-case workarounds.

What this changes (high level):
- Add FragmentCoordinator that maintains a small ledger (sequence anchor + pending fragments) per stream session.
- Introduce a deferred-toolcall mode: when a toolcall sentinel is emitted inside an unresolved fragment, the handshake is delayed until the fragment is closed or a short acknowledgement window expires.
- Emit compact "ckpt" SSE events (ckpt:<seq>) to let clients resync to last committed fragment when seeing truncated streams.
- Rework fragment flushing to use single-writer append with an epoch token to avoid interleaved delimiter slips.

Design notes / rationale:
- We chose an append-only fragment ledger (in-memory, per-session) to avoid global locks; typical session size is < 32 fragments, so memory overhead is bounded.
- Toolcall deferral is conservative: we only defer when fragment closure is ambiguous (interleaved writes, missing newline delimiter) to avoid unnecessary latency. There is a configurable window (default 50ms) for handoff.
- Checkpoints are intentionally compact strings (ckpt:<hex-seq>) to keep streaming bandwidth low and maintain OpenAI-compatible SSE event names for visibility.

Implementation details (single continuous description):
Commits: 4
- Add FragmentCoordinator and ledger implementation (streaming/fragment_coordinator.go)
- Integrate coordinator into event-emitter (streaming/emitter.go), add deferred handshake path
- Tests: unit and integration tests for fragmented JSON, toolcall deferral, checkpoint replay (streaming/*_test.go)
- Docs + changelog entry + migration note (docs/streaming-fragments.md, changelog/stream-fragment-coordinator.md)

Files changed (high level):
- services/streaming/fragment_coordinator.go (new)
- services/streaming/emitter.go (modified)
- services/streaming/fragment_coordinator_test.go (new)
- services/streaming/emitter_integration_test.go (modified)
- api/openai_compat/streaming_adapter.go (modified)
- docs/streaming-fragments.md (new)
- docs/notes/streaming-migration.md (new)
- pkg/metrics/streaming_metrics.go (modified)
- CHANGELOG.md (modified)

Behavioral changes for users:
- Clients should tolerate occasional "ckpt:<seq>" SSE events. These are informational and safe to ignore; they assist resyncing after truncation.
- Toolcall ordering guarantees are strengthened: in ambiguous fragment cases the server may delay toolcall completion until fragment closure (should be transparent for most SDKs).

Testing and QA:
- Added unit tests that simulate interleaved writes and assert the coordinator resolves fragment boundaries without producing partial JSON events.
- Streaming e2e test simulates connection truncation and verifies that clients can resync using the latest ckpt event.
- Load test: 1000 concurrent short-chat sessions; coordinator introduced <2% p90 latency increase for token emission but reduced malformed-stream incidents from ~0.7% to <0.02% in our harness.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag `enable_fragment_coordinator` and default-on for hosted API, optional for Dedicated/Private (toggleable via config).
- Canary rollout: 10% of streaming traffic for 48h, monitor malformed_streams, functioncall-duplicates, and streaming-latency metrics.
- Gradual rollout to 100% if metrics look stable.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- No protocol change required; ckpt events use SSE event names and a compact sequence id. SDKs can optionally read them for faster resync, but behavior remains compatible for clients that ignore them.

Known limitations and future work:
- The in-memory ledger doesn't persist across process restarts; in extremely long-lived sessions this could lead to a short window where resyncs are less helpful. A persisted ledger or durable checkpoint is a follow-up item.
- We intentionally set a conservative deferral window; for low-latency workloads we will expose knob tuning in the next PR.

Related tickets and prior art:
- ENG-9421: customer report of partial JSON for tool-enabled streams
- ENG-9487: internal incident postmortem recommending safer delimiter handling

Merge notes:
- Squash-merged into main after reviewer approvals and CI green. No manual conflict resolution was necessary.

review_thread: Arielle Chen: Nice approach. A couple of questions: why in-memory ledger vs. ephemeral tokens on the emitter? Please add benchmarks for p90 comparisons.
Marcus Valdez: Replied - in-memory ledger avoids cross-goroutine contentions and keeps the write path single-writer; added microbenchmarks in fragment_coordinator_test.go with p50/p90/p99 results.
Priya Nair: Please make the default deferral window configurable via env var and add a note about Dedicated/Private opt-out.
Marcus Valdez: Added feature flag and config (runtime.flag.enable_fragment_coordinator, STREAM_FRAGMENT_DEFERRAL_MS), updated docs and tests.
Liam O'Hara: Integration test flaked once on CI (timing). Please add a small retry for the e2e connection tear-down to reduce non-determinism.
Marcus Valdez: Added deterministic retry and extended test timeout by 200ms; re-ran CI.
Arielle Chen: Approved after fixes. Priya approved. Liam approved.
release_notes: Fix: improve streaming fragment resilience and avoid partial JSON/toolcall duplication. Introduces ckpt SSE events for client resync. Backwards compatible; feature flagged.
